title: Surface Area and Volume of Solids
seo_title: Surface Area and Volume – SSS 1 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Find the surface area and volume of cubes, cuboids, cylinders, cones, pyramids and spheres; solve related problems. (summary of the NERDC SSS 1 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free SSS 1 maths worksheets on mensuration of solids: volume and surface area of cylinders, cones and spheres, and word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Cone: V = ⅓πr²h; sphere: V = 4/3 πr³
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Volume of a prism or cylinder = area of the cross-section × length.
  • A cone or pyramid has one third of the volume of the matching cylinder or prism.
  • Curved surface area: cylinder 2πrh, cone πrl, sphere 4πr².

Examples

Example

Cylinder r = 7 cm, h = 10 cm

22/7 × 7 × 7 × 10

Answer: V = 1,540 cm³

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Using the slant height for the volume of a coneVolume uses the vertical height.
Forgetting the two ends of a cylinderTotal surface area = 2πrh + 2πr².
Mixing cm² and cm³Area is square units, volume is cubic units.

items.q: Two stacks of 22 coins have the same height. One stack is straight and the other leans to one side. Each coin has radius 13 mm and the stacks are 44 mm tall. How do their volumes compare?
c: The leaning stack has more volume
The straight stack has more volume
items.e: Cavalieri's principle: same height and the same cross-section at every level means the same volume. π × 13² × 44 = 7,436π. They are equal (7,436π mm³ each).

items.e: Slant height = 29 cm. TSA = CSA of cone + CSA of hemisphere = πrl + 2πr² = 4,686 cm². The joined circular faces are hidden.
